correctness.rationale: For all n≥5 and all unrestricted symmetric stochastic supported P, group averaging preserves support and symmetry and contracts ||P−J||₂. Fourier decomposition gives q(t)=1−4at−16bt(1−t) on the ordered nodes t_k. Four residue-class inequalities prove the exactly indexed maximum of g(t)=t(ℓ+r−t), and endpoint concavity proves the minimum g=ℓr. The constructed q=1−2g/d has active signs +,-,+ for n≥6, proving norm ≤ρ and exact attainment. Positive a,b and holding h are proved by four explicit factorizations, including n5. Uniqueness of orbit-constant optimum follows because any competing polynomial difference divided by t>0 is affine and cannot have endpoint nonpositive/interior nonnegative contacts without vanishing. n5 is the exact all-ones/n walk. Exact algebra gives 1−ρ=2ℓr/d=8π²n^(−2)+O(n^(−4)); nearest-only endpoint balancing gives 2π². The standalone checker passes 2446 spectral contacts, 30996 grid designs, and 3281 Fourier identity entries; a separate LP solution at n5..100 agrees to 2.3×10^(−16). Computations are corroboration, not proof. No classification of arbitrary nonuniform optimum matrices.

originality.rationale: The leading 2004 formulation encompasses the optimization abstractly, but does not state the explicit all-size two-hop-cycle solution. The 2009 primary solution is for nearest-neighbor cycles (one edge orbit), whereas the present two-edge-orbit minimax uses a middle negative Fourier contact. The 2025 same-graph spectrum is unweighted and cannot determine optimal individual transition weights by itself. The published degree-two positive trigonometric polynomial problem has a different objective/normalization. An independently verified equivalence in older literature cannot be categorically ruled out.
residual_risks: An equivalent historical cyclic band-limited Markov-chain result may exist under another term despite the material primary comparisons.
The general FMMC SDP literature covers computation at each finite n but not necessarily a published closed-form all-size theorem; another specialized paper could have evaluated it.
The finite numerical LP and checker support but cannot establish originality or independently certify the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Selecting fastest stochastic consensus weights on two-hop circular networks is a natural extension of the classical one-hop ring, and exact all-size optimization is not determined by the known unweighted spectrum. The result supplies a fully realizable strictly positive two-edge-type/holding design, a three-frequency active-set rule, and a sharp factor-four spectral-gap improvement at large size. It is a structural design law, not an arbitrary finite numerical recomputation or a trivial parameter substitution. It does not claim exact finite-time total-variation speedup.
